How does your bank's efficiency compare?

Your bank's efficiency ratio, assets and loans per employee, against peers of the same size in the same state. Public FDIC Call Report data, refreshed every quarter.

Loading public FDIC data…

Method

How the comparison works

Where do the numbers come from?

The FDIC's public BankFind Suite, which publishes each bank's quarterly Call Report financials. We refresh the page when the FDIC publishes a new quarter, usually about eight weeks after quarter end.

Who counts as a peer?

Banks in the same state and the same total-asset band: under $300 million, $300 million to $1 billion, $1 to $3 billion, $3 to $10 billion, and over $10 billion.

What is the efficiency ratio?

Noninterest expense divided by revenue (net interest income plus noninterest income), as reported by the FDIC. Lower means less expense for each dollar of revenue. Strategy, mix of business and investment cycles all move it, so treat it as a starting point for a question, not a verdict.

Do you see what I search for?

No. The whole dataset loads into your browser and the lookup happens there. Nothing you type is sent anywhere.

Want this in your board pack, or wired into your own reporting?

A working session is 20 minutes with the engineer who would build it. Bring the report your team assembles by hand each quarter.
